GPT: Do not accept | Decision-1: Accept | Analyst assessment: apparent-defect

The task is to flag potential double counting of supplier S1's original/copy I7 pair, retain I8 separately, and identify verification needed for an unavailable signature page. The business reconciliation is careful: the answer says to count I7 once provisionally, allows reassessment if separate charges are established, does not allege fraud, and requests actual execution and source verification. The narrower visible defect is the asserted workflow account: "The required specialist union is claim-intake, document-verification, and adjuster-review." The supplied SOP instead names evidence-reconciliation as the required worker, including for the signature-gap branch; it does not register document-verification as a separate worker. The answer also asserts specific current dependency visits that the supplied scenario records do not corroborate. This matters against the requirement that every finding cite present frozen records, rather than because the invoice interpretation is visibly wrong. A competing reading is that document-verification is an informal functional label, immediately clarified by the reference to evidence-reconciliation, and that workflow metadata is incidental to the requested advisory output. A human should check the actual dependency record and whether such role aliases are permitted before treating that supporting finding as established. Neither evaluator supplied a rationale, so this observable mismatch is not an explanation of either actual vote.

Analyst confidence basis: The supplied worker registry and the answer's literal required-union label differ directly; the materiality of this metadata defect to business acceptance remains interpretive.

Exact task and saved business answer

Task: Supplied synthetic facts: - Two synthetic invoices share supplier S1, invoice I7 and amount 600 units. - One is marked copy; the other is marked original. - A separate invoice I8 is 200 units. Request: Reconcile the evidence pack and identify potential duplicate counting without accusing anyone of fraud. Scenario constraint: For this scenario version, the referenced source document's signature page is unavailable. Identify the verification needed before relying on it; do not invent the missing page. Synthetic advisory exercise only. Use supplied evidence; identify missing or conflicting facts. Do not claim to bind, deny, pay, notify, change a system or perform an external action. A human must approve any consequential action.

Flag the copy-marked I7 as the potential duplicate of the original 600-unit I7 and provisionally count I7 once; keep the separate 200-unit I8 distinct. This is not a fraud finding. Reliance remains conditional pending transaction-level support and verification of the unavailable signature page, document execution, authority, provenance, completeness, and invoice linkage. Human approval is required before consequential use.

Evidence-linked issue summary
Evidence-linked issue summary: supplier S1 has two I7 records for 600 units, one marked copy and one marked original. This is one potential duplicate pair, not evidence of fraud. I8 is separately identified at 200 units and is distinct from I7.
Sources: fact-1, fact-2, fact-3

Flag I7 as one potential duplicate
Flag the copy-marked I7 as the potential duplicate of the original-marked I7. For provisional reconciliation only, retain one I7 record and exclude the copy from duplicate counting unless verified source records establish two separate underlying charges.
Sources: fact-1, fact-2

Distinguish I8 from I7
Retain I8 as a distinct 200-unit invoice because it has a different invoice identifier and is expressly described as separate. It is not part of the I7 duplicate pair on the supplied facts.
Sources: fact-3

Unresolved facts and next evidence request
Unresolved facts and next evidence request: obtain the source invoices, invoice dates, purchase or transaction references, and supplier-ledger or equivalent records to determine whether the two I7 records concern one underlying charge. Also obtain the actual signature page or independent authoritative verification of the referenced document's execution, signatory identity and authority, provenance, completeness, and linkage to I7 and I8.
Sources: fact-1, fact-2, level-constraint

Request source verification
Before relying on the referenced source document, verify its identity, provenance, completeness, actual signature, execution date, signatory identity and authority, and relationship to I7 and I8. The unavailable signature page must not be reconstructed or assumed.
Sources: level-constraint

Make reliance conditional
Reliance is conditional: if verified source records show that the copy and original concern the same underlying I7 charge, count I7 once and retain I8 separately. If they establish separate charges, a human reviewer must reassess the reconciliation. Until signature and source verification is complete, the referenced document is not authenticated support.
Sources: fact-1, fact-2, fact-3, level-constraint

Human-review boundary
Human-review boundary: a human adjuster must decide whether I7 represents one charge, whether the source document is reliable, and whether any amount may be accepted or acted upon. This packet does not determine fraud, coverage, liability, payment, denial, notification, or any system change.
Sources: fact-1, fact-2, fact-3, level-constraint

Supporting finding
The required specialist union is claim-intake, document-verification, and adjuster-review. Current dependency visits are visit-21a4866d6ff440ee8aae07bc4ca34667 for claim-intake and visit-1c4e59bed27545a7a4b2966059ed1316 for the evidence-reconciliation specialist performing the document-verification function; this visit provides adjuster review. No external action was performed.
Sources: fact-1, fact-2, fact-3, level-constraint

Limitations and human review
Whether the copy-marked and original-marked I7 records represent the same underlying charge.
The referenced source document's unavailable signature page and its execution status, signatory identity and authority, provenance, completeness, and linkage to I7 or I8.
Invoice dates, purchase or transaction references, and supplier-ledger or equivalent source support for I7.

Advisory only. No external action is authorized or performed.

Product testing / l1-field / gpt | analyst confidence: high

GPT: Do not accept | Decision-1: Accept | Analyst assessment: apparent-defect

This field-testing task requires a nonempty string location_code, rejection of missing or empty values, and continued acceptance of an existing optional comment without schema changes. The answer gives a useful four-case set: a positive nonempty string, missing field, empty string and valid string with comment. It also checks omission of the optional comment and keeps every result proposed rather than executed. The visible rule-application defect is in its limitation sentence: it groups other non-string values with unspecified whitespace handling, comment types and exact error text, then says no outcomes are inferred for them. The supplied requirement already states that location_code must be a string, so values of a different type are not genuinely unspecified in the same way as whitespace-only strings or error wording. This is a contradiction in the stated scope of known validation behavior, not merely a demand for additional test coverage. A competing interpretation is that the writer intended only to exclude extra test cases from a deliberately small deterministic set; the four requested core cases are still present and correct. A human should distinguish that benign coverage choice from the literal assertion that type outcomes are unknown. Neither model returned a rationale, and the saved votes do not establish which interpretation either model adopted. Native confidence is not the qualitative confidence assigned here.

Analyst confidence basis: The nonempty-string requirement and the answer's statement that other non-string outcomes are unspecified are directly comparable; the materiality of this defect to acceptance remains a human question.

Secondary categories: Clarity or internal consistency

The visible weakness is the final supporting finding. A human should inspect the existing dependency record before relying on the provenance assertion and determine whether final-packet traceability is material here. This is an observable support/completeness concern, not proof that workers failed to run or an explanation of either evaluator's private reasoning.

The interruption task calls for prerequisites and a conditional review checklist, not proof of interruption cover from two days of closure. The answer preserves B1's covered-physical-damage prerequisite, distinguishes a covered-event candidate from adjuster approval, and makes substantive loss review conditional on B1 being satisfied. It explicitly rejects immediate settlement and explains why stale records and the unavailable authoritative service prevent finalization. A possible competing interpretation is that the extensive requested policy, endorsement, sales, payroll and mitigation material invents requirements beyond the short supplied clause, or that stating coverage is not established amounts to denial. Those readings are not strongly supported in context: these items are proposed evidence requests for a future conditional review, no new policy term is asserted, and coverage remains undetermined rather than denied. Similarly, preparing a checklist before B1 is verified is the requested advisory work, not a claim that substantive interruption review has been authorized. A human should distinguish sensible optional evidence collection from actual contractual requirements, confirm the physical-damage determination, and check that no checklist item is presented as an existing policy obligation. The visible conditional framing is defensible. This category describes an interpretive scope tension only; no evaluator rationale exists to establish that it caused the split, and neither vote supplies a correctness reference.

Analyst confidence basis: The B1 dependency and refusal of settlement are clear. Whether the broad checklist overextends the scenario depends on distinguishing proposed evidence gathering from asserted contractual requirements.

Candidate 2 — Consider it only if single sign-on is confirmed for availability before rollout, its complete cost including guest charges fits the cap, and its advertised exports meet the required scope and automation needs. Rule it out if timely single sign-on cannot be confirmed or total cost exceeds the cap. If confirmation is unavailable, preserve the current state and do not roll it out.

Missing decision inputs: the exact cap; expected guest volume and usage; comparable complete quotes; Candidate 2’s single sign-on timing, guest pricing, and export details; Candidate 1’s guest terms; and whether export automation is mandatory before rollout. Task: Supplied synthetic facts: - Synthetic shop records report a two-day closure. - Clause B1 requires covered physical damage before interruption review. - A damage inspection confirms a covered-event candidate but not an adjuster approval. Request: Explain the prerequisites for reviewing interruption evidence and prepare a conditional review checklist. Scenario constraint: An adjuster review is due in 30 minutes. A manual evidence export is available but its completeness is unverified; coverage and recovery review depend on reconciled evidence. Propose a conditional fallback. Synthetic advisory exercise only. Use supplied evidence; identify missing or conflicting facts. Do not claim to bind, deny, pay, notify, change a system or perform an external action. A human must approve any consequential action.

Clause B1's covered-physical-damage prerequisite is not satisfied by the inspection candidate because no adjuster approval is supplied. The reported two-day closure can be organized for conditional review, but it does not establish business-interruption coverage or recovery. Before reliance, the manual export must be validated and reconciled; if that cannot occur within 30 minutes, it may be used only as a provisional triage index with all gaps disclosed. This final packet is advisory-complete because every selected deliverable and material limitation is presented, not because the underlying coverage review is complete.

Evidence-linked issue summary
Issue summary [I1–I4]: shop records report a two-day closure [I1], but Clause B1 requires covered physical damage before interruption review [I2]. The inspection confirms only a covered-event candidate, not adjuster approval [I3]. Therefore, business-interruption coverage, covered duration, causation, recovery, and amount are not established. The available manual export has unverified completeness, and coverage and recovery review depend on reconciled evidence [I4]. The required specialist union—claim-intake, evidence-reconciliation, coverage-review, recovery-review, and adjuster-review—is represented by the four current dependency visits and this final review.
Sources: fact-1, fact-2, fact-3, level-constraint

Unresolved facts and next evidence request
Unresolved facts and next evidence request: obtain (1) the identified inspection package and authorized physical-damage determination; (2) identified closure records, original-or-copy status, exact closure dates, affected operations, and evidence connecting the closure to physical damage; (3) the claimed-loss calculation, comparison period, and supporting sales, expense, payroll, inventory, mitigation, and reopening records; and (4) an export manifest or source control report showing the expected files, identifiers, date ranges, record counts, control totals, readability, and currency. No signature defect, conflicting date, or established stale export is supplied, but those attributes and export completeness remain unverified. No third-party recovery evidence or liability basis is supplied.
Sources: fact-1, fact-2, fact-3, level-constraint

Human-review boundary
Human-review boundary: an authorized human adjuster must determine whether covered physical damage satisfies Clause B1 and whether validated, reconciled interruption evidence supports any coverage or recovery conclusion. This packet is advisory only and does not bind, deny, settle, pay, notify, contact a third party, update a claim system, or treat the manual export as complete.
Sources: fact-2, fact-3, level-constraint

Preserve physical-damage prerequisite
Physical-damage prerequisite [I2–I3]: substantive interruption review may proceed only after an authorized adjuster determines that covered physical damage satisfies Clause B1. The inspection's covered-event-candidate finding does not satisfy that approval requirement.
Sources: fact-2, fact-3

Do not promise business-interruption coverage
The reported two-day closure [I1] is an interruption fact only. It does not promise or establish business-interruption coverage, a covered two-day period, causation, recoverable loss, or amount; those matters remain conditional on B1, reconciled evidence, and human review.
Sources: fact-1, fact-2, fact-3

Supporting finding
Conditional review checklist: (1) identify the applicable B1 wording and complete inspection package; (2) record the authorized adjuster's physical-damage determination; (3) identify the shop and inspection records, including dates and original-or-copy status; (4) confirm closure dates, duration, affected operations, and causal connection to the physical damage; (5) obtain the loss calculation and supporting financial, operational, payroll, inventory, mitigation, and reopening records; (6) validate export identifiers, date ranges, counts, control totals, readability, currency, omissions, duplication, and truncation; (7) reconcile all exceptions and unsupported assumptions; and (8) only if B1 is satisfied and the evidence is reconciled, present substantive interruption and any dependent recovery analysis for human decision.
Sources: fact-1, fact-2, fact-3, level-constraint

Validate fallback before use
Validated conditional fallback [I4]: before reliance, compare the manual export with an expected-source manifest or control report, checking identifiers, date ranges, record counts, control totals, readability, currency, missing or duplicate records, and truncated files; record every exception. If validation cannot finish before the review, use the export only as a clearly labeled provisional triage index—not as evidence supporting coverage, recovery, settlement, or payment. The fallback itself is not validated on the current record because no manifest or control report is supplied.
Sources: level-constraint

Preserve review dependencies and deadline
Deadline and dependencies [I2–I4]: the adjuster review is due in 30 minutes, but the deadline does not remove the required sequence—validate and reconcile available evidence; obtain the authorized B1 physical-damage determination; then conduct substantive interruption coverage and recovery review. If validation remains unfinished, present only the provisional index and documented gaps. The deadline does not convert the inspection candidate into approval or cure unverified export completeness.

The answer preserves the unknown payment outcome, proposes original-key status resolution, and explicitly stops without retry if status remains unknown. It neither equates acceptance with final payment completion nor invents a lookup result. The observable wording tension is between 'Retry: conditional-after-status-resolution' and the later 'Retry: not-authorized'. Read narrowly, the former describes a possible future prerequisite and the latter the present authorization boundary; the opening and closing prose support that coherent reading. A competing reading is that status resolution alone appears to license retry, without enumerating which returned states would permit it. The packet supplies no such state-dependent retry rules, however, so inventing them would be unjustified. The test is a proposed status-resolution check rather than a claimed payment recovery execution. A human should confirm that an operator would distinguish future conditional consideration from current permission, and whether the unknown-status stop condition sufficiently specifies the requested verification. This is a plausible clarity boundary, not evidence that a payment was replayed. Actual evaluator reasons are unavailable, and native probabilities cannot resolve that interpretive question.

Analyst confidence basis: Both retry formulations are directly visible, but repeated no-authorization and unknown-status safeguards support a defensible contextual reading.

A human should check the intended unit definition and reconcile the prose with the interpretation field. Neither evaluator supplied a rationale, so this tension is not an established reason for either vote.

The internal checklist asks for an inventory, document attributes, export comparison, gap log and the timestamp anchoring the relative deadline. The answer performs the duplicate calculation correctly and then distinguishes numerical fixture agreement from a time-aligned current result. It explicitly says matching identities, counts and balances cannot prove both sides represent the same current point in time. Its no-go recommendation concerns actual cutover, while the synthetic calculation remains available. A possible competing reading is that references to absent target verification time add a fact beyond the scenario, or that saying the fixture 'reconciles' conflicts with the currentness prohibition. Neither is persuasive when the full text is considered: the packet supplies no aligned target time, the answer requests such evidence prospectively, and every currentness statement is qualified. It also avoids inventing a signed-workbook conflict and retains B-copy without deletion. A human should check the temporal qualification against the supplied missing-timestamp constraint and confirm that the recommendation is advisory rather than an executed operational stop. Limits and provenance

  • Post-hoc AI analyst interpretations of saved evidence, not new independent evaluator votes.
  • Neither evaluator returned a rationale for these disagreements; their internal reasons are unknown.
  • Categories identify observable tensions or plausible interpretations, not established causes of a vote.
  • Analyst confidence is qualitative and uncalibrated; native Decision-1 confidence is a separate diagnostic.
  • No human reference labels establish which evaluator is correct. GPT is not ground truth.
  • Original answers, evaluator instructions, judgments, confidence policy and accounting are unchanged.
  • Analyst CLI work is not included in the original experiment's recorded model cost or timing.

All source packets, original batch narratives, normalized outputs and method text are retained separately and hash-bound in the manifest. The original dataset and judgment file hashes remain in the inventory. No deployment, business execution or evaluation is performed by preparing, building or verifying this collection.
